Faculty Resource Center Refresh

The Research Support Office has refreshed the Faculty Resource Center to make it easier for faculty to find and access key research support resources. The site includes information on pre- and post-award services, funding opportunities, proposal development, broader impacts, and current RSO initiatives.

Visit the Faculty Resource Center to explore resources designed to support your research success.

Research Funding Opportunities

Office of Naval Research

October 30, 2026 | Young Investigator Program (YIP)
The Office of Naval Research (ONR) has released the FY 2027 Young Investigator Program (YIP), a highly competitive opportunity supporting early-career faculty through multi-year research awards. This year’s solicitation aligns with ONR’s updated science and technology focus areas, including AI and autonomy, advanced materials, manufacturing, energy, aerospace, undersea systems and more.
 
Eligible applicants must hold a tenure-track or equivalent faculty position and have earned a PhD on or after Jan. 1, 2019. Faculty considering submission should contact Bill Doe and are strongly encouraged to connect with the relevant ONR program officer before applying.
 
November 16, 2026 | Communications and Networking Applied Research Opportunity
The Office of Naval Research (ONR) is seeking applied research proposals that advance communications and networking capabilities in support of the Navy’s Information Warfare mission. Areas of interest include resilient communications, advanced antennas, distributed network control, traffic engineering and low-probability-of-detection technologies. While not required, white papers are strongly encouraged and should be submitted as early as possible. Full proposals are due Nov. 16, 2026. Faculty interested in this opportunity are encouraged to review the solicitation and engage with ONR program officers early in the process.

National Science Foundation

NSF Funding Opportunities for Foundational Research
Full Proposals Accepted Anytime | Target Submission Dates Vary by Program
The National Science Foundation (NSF) has announced a suite of 12 new Notices of Funding Opportunities (NOFOs) supporting foundational research across the sciences and engineering. Collectively, these opportunities represent more than $1.5 billion in potential funding for basic and use-inspired research that advances discovery, innovation, and societal impact.

Proposals may be submitted at any time; however, investigators are strongly encouraged to submit by the target dates established by individual programs to ensure consideration during the appropriate review cycle.

The new opportunities span a wide range of disciplines, including:

CISE: Expeditions in Computing
Supports the pursuit of ambitious, foundational research agendas that promise to define the future of computing and information.

ENG: Electrical, Communications, and Computing Systems (ECCS)
Supports foundational research for electrical, communications and computing systems.

ENG: Civil, Mechanical and Manufacturing Innovation (CMMI)
Supports foundational research projects for civil, mechanical, and manufacturing innovation.

ENG: Chemical, Bioengineering, Energy and Transport Systems (CBET)
Supports foundational engineering research for chemical, bioengineering, energy, and transport systems.

ENG: Emerging Frontiers in Research and Innovation: Wave-Based Computing
Supports foundational and transformative research to advance the development of computing approaches that harness the principles of wave dynamics.

GEO: Geosciences Core Research: Atmospheric, Geospace, Earth and Ocean Sciences
Supports foundational research projects that advance the frontiers of knowledge across all areas of the geosciences.

MPS Mathematical Sciences Research Programs (MPS MathSci)
Supports multiple research programs at the frontiers of discovery in theoretical and applied mathematical sciences.

MPS Materials Research Programs (MPS Materials)
Supports multiple materials research programs that advance fundamental understanding of materials, their properties, and their potential applications.

MPS Physics Research Programs (MPS Physics)
Supports multiple research programs at the frontiers of discovery in physics.

MPS Chemistry Research Programs (MPS Chem)
Supports multiple disciplinary research programs in chemistry that connect molecular-level understanding to advances across different domains.

MPS Astronomical Sciences Research Programs (MPS Astro)
Supports foundational astronomical sciences research and instrumentation focused on exploring space and advancing fundamental understanding of the universe.

Note: Biomechanics and Mechanobiology (BMMB) program and the Mechanics of Materials and Structures (MoMs) program are now part of the Mechanics of Advanced Materials System (MAMS) program. Translational and Commercialization Funding

NSF Translation to Practice-Explore (TTP-E) ($600,000)
Rolling Deadline
The NSF TTP-E track provides the opportunity to obtain an extension of the initial award period of a current NSF award for up to two years in order to offer investigators an opportunity to explore adventurous, high-risk, use-inspired research and initial translational activities as the starting point for translation that was not covered by the original research award.

NREL Innovation & Entrepreneurship Center: Active Funding Opportunities
Deadlines Vary
The NREL Innovation and Entrepreneurship Center curates and maintains this evolving list of active opportunities for energy, built environment, fuels and chemicals, manufacturing, natural resources, climate management, transportation and mobility, and water and wastewater technology translation.

SBIR/STTR Commercialization Grant Programs
Rolling Application Deadline
Through the Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) and Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) programs, America’s Seed Fund awards non-dilutive funding to develop your technology and chart a path toward commercialization. Participating Agencies: NSF, DOE, USDA, DOD, NASA, EPA, DOT, DHS, HHS, Department of Education, and Department of Commerce. Phase I: $50,000-275,000; Phase II: $750,000-$1.8M.

Upcoming Events

2026 National Postdoc Appreciation Week

The Office of Postdoctoral Affairs (OPA) will recognize Outstanding Postdocs and Outstanding Mentors during National Postdoc Appreciation Week (NPAW), Sept. 21-25. NPAW celebrates the important research, teaching and service contributions of postdoctoral scholars. This year's celebration will feature a variety of in-person and virtual events designed to support and recognize the campus postdoc community.

Webinar: Applying to the Early Career Fellowship

Wednesday, Nov. 11, Noon-1 p.m., Virtual
Previous fellows will share their successful experiences and be available to answer questions. The Early Career Fellowships are a limited submission funding opportunity, requiring an internal competition to determine the applicant(s) that will submit proposals. This workshop will be a great opportunity to learn about how to put together a competitive proposal in advance of the internal competition deadline.

Announcements

Chancellor’s Postdoctoral Fellowship

The Chancellor’s Postdoctoral Fellowship Program supports the recruitment and development of outstanding postdoctoral scholars on campus. Beginning with the 2026 application cycle, each school or college may nominate a limited number of candidates for campus-level consideration. The College of Engineering may nominate up to two candidates.

RSO White Paper on Industry Research Priorities

Industry partnerships account for ~10% of college research but play an outsized role in connecting faculty work to real-world applications. The Research Support Office’s white paper, "Anticipating Industry Research Directions,” outlines key themes shaping industry priorities over the next 5–10 years, supporting strategic decisions around seed funding, faculty hiring, and partnership growth in emerging technology areas.

Have ideas or success stories to share? PIs are encouraged to submit insights, lessons learned, or examples of successful strategies for consideration in the weekly RSO newsletter. Submit contributions to Bill Doe, Research Development Manager (RSO).
